policy_title: Introduce Triple Lock Plus for Pensioners
stated: The Conservative Party will introduce a new Triple Lock Plus, guaranteeing that both the State Pension and the tax-free allowance for pensioners always rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%, ensuring the new State Pension does not get dragged into income tax.

source.quote: Cut tax for pensioners with the new Triple Lock Plus, guaranteeing that both the State Pension and the tax free allowance for pensioners always rise with the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5% – so the new State Pension doesn’t get dragged into income tax.

bearing_set.reason: Directly affects pensioner income adequacy by uprating both the State Pension and a pensioner-specific personal allowance, materially reducing the risk of pensioner poverty and tax drag on retirement income.
The policy affects real disposable income for pensioners by ensuring their tax-free threshold rises alongside the pension, preventing fiscal drag from eroding their effective take-home income.

Extending the triple-lock guarantee to the personal allowance is a tax-threshold measure that determines how much of their pension income pensioners keep; it directly reduces the household tax burden for pensioners whose pension approaches the current frozen allowance.

Uprating the personal allowance in line with the triple-lock formula forgoes income-tax revenue from pensioners; if unfunded, this widens the fiscal gap — a concrete mechanism acting on the funded-vs-borrowed indicator (IFS estimated the commitment costs ~£1–2bn p.a.).

membership_note: Three distinct, non-negligible bearings: O8 (net pensioner income/security), O11 (personal-allowance tax burden), and O12 (revenue cost and fiscal sustainability). O14 was considered but the distributional direction within the broader population is ambiguous and does not clearly meet the non-negligible bar compared with the three included.
